sentences.en: Some Thieves broke into a house, and found nothing worth taking except a Cock, which they seized and carried off with them.
sentences.zh: 几个盗贼闯进一户人家，除了一只公鸡，没找到什么值得拿的东西，便抓了它带着走了。

sentences.en: When they were preparing their supper, one of them caught up the Cock …
sentences.zh: 他们准备晚饭时，其中一个抓起公鸡……

sentences.en: … and was about to wring his neck, when he cried out for mercy and said, "Pray do not kill me …
sentences.zh: ……正要拧断它的脖子，公鸡求饶道：「请别杀我……」

sentences.en: … you will find me a most useful bird, for I rouse honest men to their work in the morning by my crowing."
sentences.zh: 「……您会发现我是只很有用的鸟，早上我靠打鸣把老实人叫起来干活。」

sentences.en: But the Thief replied with some heat, "Yes, I know you do, making it still harder for us to get a livelihood.
sentences.zh: 可那盗贼有些激动地答道：「是啊，我知道你干这事，这让我们更没法谋生了。

sentences.en: Into the pot you go!"
sentences.zh: 进锅去吧！」

sentences.en: A hungry Fox found in a hollow tree a quantity of bread and meat, which some shepherds had placed there against their return.
sentences.zh: 一只饥饿的狐狸在空心树里发现了一些面包和肉，是几个牧人放在那里留着回来吃的。

sentences.en: Delighted with his find he slipped in through the narrow aperture and greedily devoured it all.
sentences.zh: 它得此发现喜出望外，从窄窄的洞口中钻进去，贪婪地吃了个精光。

sentences.en: But when he tried to get out again he found himself so swollen after his big meal that he could not squeeze through the hole …
sentences.zh: 可当它想再钻出来时，发现饱餐之后肚子胀得那么厉害，怎么也挤不出那个洞了……

sentences.en: … and fell to whining and groaning over his misfortune.
sentences.zh: ……便为自己的倒霉哀声叹气起来。

sentences.en: Another Fox, happening to pass that way, came and asked him what the matter was …
sentences.zh: 另一只狐狸恰好路过，走过来问它怎么了……

sentences.en: … and, on learning the state of the case, said, "Well, my friend, I see nothing for it but for you to stay where you are till you shrink …
sentences.zh: ……弄清原委后说：「唉，朋友，我看没别的办法，你只能待在那儿等瘦下来……」

sentences.en: … to your former size; you'll get out then easily enough."
sentences.zh: 「……瘦回原来的样子，那时要出来就容易了。」

sentences.en: A Peasant had an Apple-tree growing in his garden, which bore no fruit …
sentences.zh: 一个农夫园子里长着一棵苹果树，它不结果子……

sentences.en: … but merely served to provide a shelter from the heat for the sparrows and grasshoppers which sat and chirped in its branches.
sentences.zh: ……只是给在枝头栖着鸣叫的麻雀和蚱蜢遮遮暑气。

sentences.en: Disappointed at its barrenness he determined to cut it down, and went and fetched his axe for the purpose.
sentences.zh: 他嫌它不结果，便决定砍掉它，为此去取了斧头。

sentences.en: But when the sparrows and the grasshoppers saw what he was about to do, they begged him to spare it …
sentences.zh: 可麻雀和蚱蜢见他要动手，便求他放过这棵树……

sentences.en: … and said to him, "If you destroy the tree we shall have to seek shelter elsewhere …
sentences.zh: ……对他说：「您若毁掉这棵树，我们就得另找栖身之处……」

sentences.en: … and you will no longer have our merry chirping to enliven your work in the garden."
sentences.zh: 「……您在园里干活时，也就再没有我们欢快的鸣叫作伴了。」

sentences.en: He, however, refused to listen to them, and set to work with a will to cut through the trunk.
sentences.zh: 可他不肯听，劲头十足地动手去砍树干。

sentences.en: A few strokes showed that it was hollow inside and contained a swarm of bees and a large store of honey.
sentences.zh: 砍了几斧，便看出里面是空的，藏着一窝蜜蜂和大量蜂蜜。

sentences.en: Delighted with his find he threw down his axe, saying, "The old tree is worth keeping after all."
sentences.zh: 他因这发现大喜，扔下斧头说：「这棵老树终究还是值得留着的。」

sentences.en: Utility is most men's test of worth.
sentences.zh: 对多数人来说，有用才算有价值。

sentences.en: A Jackdaw, watching some Pigeons in a farmyard, was filled with envy when he saw how well they were fed …
sentences.zh: 一只寒鸦看着农家院子里的几只鸽子，见它们吃得多好，满心羡慕……

sentences.en: … and determined to disguise himself as one of them, in order to secure a share of the good things they enjoyed.
sentences.zh: ……便决意伪装成它们中的一员，好分得一份它们享受的好处。

sentences.en: So he painted himself white from head to foot and joined the flock …
sentences.zh: 于是他从头到脚把自己涂成白色，混进了鸽群……

sentences.en: … and, so long as he was silent, they never suspected that he was not a pigeon like themselves.
sentences.zh: ……只要他不作声，鸽子们从没怀疑过他其实不是同类。

sentences.en: But one day he was unwise enough to start chattering …
sentences.zh: 可是有一天他不小心开口叫了起来……

sentences.en: … when they at once saw through his disguise and pecked him so unmercifully that he was glad to escape and join his own kind again.
sentences.zh: ……鸽子们立刻看穿了他的伪装，毫不留情地啄他，他只好赶紧逃回去找同类。

sentences.en: But the other jackdaws did not recognise him in his white dress, and would not let him feed with them, but drove him away …
sentences.zh: 可别的寒鸦认不出他这身白装，不让他一起觅食，把他赶走了……

sentences.en: … and so he became a homeless wanderer for his pains.
sentences.zh: ……于是他白费心机，成了无家可归的流浪者。

sentences.en: Jupiter was about to marry a wife, and determined to celebrate the event by inviting all the animals to a banquet.
sentences.zh: 朱庇特要娶妻了，决定宴请所有动物来庆祝这件喜事。

sentences.en: They all came except the Tortoise, who did not put in an appearance, much to Jupiter's surprise.
sentences.zh: 大家都来了，唯独乌龟没有露面，这让朱庇特很意外。

sentences.en: So when he next saw the Tortoise he asked him why he had not been at the banquet.
sentences.zh: 所以下次见到乌龟时，他便问它为什么没来赴宴。

sentences.en: "I don't care for going out," said the Tortoise; "there's no place like home."
sentences.zh: 「我不爱出门，」乌龟说，「哪儿都不如家里好。」

sentences.en: Jupiter was so much annoyed by this reply that he decreed that from that time forth the Tortoise should carry his house upon his back …
sentences.zh: 朱庇特被这个回答弄得很恼火，便规定从今往后乌龟要把房子背在背上……

sentences.en: … and never be able to get away from home even if he wished to.
sentences.zh: ……即便想离开家也永远走不脱了。
